articles.topic: CSO Sustainable Mobility and Transport 2024: EV running-cost motives and home-charging access
articles.distinct_thesis: The new survey shows lower running costs influenced more EV owners than environmental benefit, while home charging became materially more important; a worked comparison shows why the saving depends on mileage and charging mix rather than the drivetrain label alone.

claim_checks.claim: Running affordability influenced 72.1%, environmental contribution 59.4%, reduced motor tax 34.4%, home charging 24.4%, grants 20.1% and public charging 6.3% of surveyed EV owners.
claim_checks.basis: CSO release published 20 November 2026; multiple responses were allowed.

claim_checks.claim: Home charging rose from 10.4% in 2021 to 24.4% in 2024, a 14-point or approximately 2.35-times increase.
Illustrative 15,000km annual energy cost is €637.50 for a 17kWh/100km EV at €0.25/kWh and €1,665 for a 6L/100km petrol car at €1.85/L.
claim_checks.basis: 2,550kWh × €0.25 = €637.50; 900L × €1.85 = €1,665. Prices and efficiencies are explicitly labelled assumptions, not market averages.

articles.topic: Central Bank Financial Stability Review 2026:II mortgage repayment stress scenarios
articles.distinct_thesis: The Central Bank's scenarios show that most exposed borrowers would see modest changes but a material tail could face increases above €200; the analysis explains the denominator and stress assumptions so a scenario is not mistaken for a forecast.

claim_checks.claim: 57% of PDH borrowers at retail banks are exposed to near-term rate changes through SVR, tracker or a fixed rate expiring within a year.
claim_checks.basis: Central Bank Financial Stability Review 2026:II, page 37.

claim_checks.claim: A 100bp shock puts about 14% of the exposed group in the €100–€200 increase band and just under 7% above €200; at 200bp the figures are 28% and 20%.
claim_checks.basis: Central Bank stress scenario; article states full pass-through and that this is not a forecast.

claim_checks.claim: A €250,000 repayment mortgage over 20 years rises from €1,449.90 at 3.5% to €1,581.62 at 4.5% and €1,719.72 at 5.5%.
claim_checks.basis: Standard monthly amortisation formula, constant rate, no fees or overpayments.

articles.topic: Employment Permits Portal outage: limited alternative-process test and practical applicant guidance
articles.distinct_thesis: The 19 November recovery step is limited testing rather than a general reopening; the service article separates the actions for submitted, draft, new, renewal and appeal cases and preserves the distinction between flexibility and a legal deadline extension.

claim_checks.claim: The Department began testing a temporary alternative process with a limited number of companies while the portal remains unavailable.
New applications cannot generally be submitted by email; review and appeal applications remain subject to the 28-day deadline and can use EPreviews@enterprise.gov.ie.
claim_checks.basis: Official portal service FAQ; article does not describe limited company testing as universal access.

claim_checks.claim: The 20 November processing-date snapshot showed 23 October for Critical Skills, General and other new applications; 22 October for ICT new; 16 October for ICT renewals; 14 October for other renewals; and 6 May for reviews/appeals.
claim_checks.basis: Official current application processing dates page, captured as a dated queue snapshot rather than a completion promise.
